main.title: Yoshi's Crafted World
main.subtitle: Cardboard, Glue and Depth Become Level Design
main.summary: Yoshi’s Crafted World uses the backs of its handmade stages to turn familiar places into a different search.

cards.heading: A world made from ordinary materials
cards.text: Yoshi's Crafted World launched on Nintendo Switch on 29 March 2019. Good-Feel built its stages from the appearance of paper, cartons, cups and other household materials. The Yoshis pursue the scattered gems of the Sundream Stone, with a landscape that openly shows how its scenery has been assembled.

cards.heading: Walk around to the other side
cards.text: The Flip Side turns most stages around, exposing the backs of their props. The new objective is to locate three hidden Poochy Pups and reach the end quickly. A route already crossed becomes another search because changing the view reveals objects that the front-facing composition concealed.

cards.heading: Bring another Yoshi
cards.text: Two players can share the adventure, with one Yoshi carrying another on its back. Mellow Mode adds wings to help clear obstacles. These options allow different approaches to the same spaces. The handmade style supports both: a stage can be an obstacle course, a small scavenger hunt or something to explore together.

cards.heading: Finding crafted souvenirs for the Blockafellers
cards.text: Blockafellers appear in each subworld to provide the Yoshis with missions to find souvenirs in the form of crafts, themed decorations that appear in the foreground or background. One at a time, Yoshi will be requested to find a certain number of the souvenir in a certain level. Once Yoshi finds and throws eggs at each of them, he can leave the level immediately, or continue to play through. Either way, after returning to the world map, the Blockafeller will give Yoshi a Smiley Flower as a reward and, if there are still uncollected souvenirs in the subworld, request another type of souvenir.

main.title: Anno 1800
main.subtitle: Building an industrial city
main.summary: Anno 1800 is a 2019 city-building game in which production chains, population needs and trade routes drive the growth of an industrial city.

cards.heading: A city at the start of the industrial age
cards.text: Anno 1800 is Ubisoft Blue Byte?s city-building game set at the beginning of the industrial age. Released on April 16, 2019, it connects housing, factories, trade and expeditions. A growing city needs enough workers, roads, warehouses and raw materials to keep its industries supplied.

cards.heading: Balancing production chains
cards.text: Many goods require several production stages: grain becomes flour, then bread. More advanced products add further inputs and worker requirements. Players balance these chains by adjusting production and transport when one link cannot meet demand.

cards.heading: Population and changing needs
cards.text: Farmers, workers, artisans, engineers and investors fill different roles and demand different goods. Upgrading residences changes both the available workforce and what the population consumes. A larger, wealthier city therefore needs an increasingly varied supply network.

cards.heading: Trade between islands
cards.text: Automated trade routes carry resources between island ports. Other regions and expeditions provide materials unavailable at home, making ships part of the production chain. Players must account for travel time and cargo capacity when supplying their cities.

main.title: BoxBoy! + BoxGirl!
main.subtitle: A few boxes can become a route
main.summary: BoxBoy! + BoxGirl! is HAL Laboratory's puzzle-platform game, released for Nintendo Switch on 26 April 2019.

cards.heading: A few boxes can become a route
cards.text: BoxBoy! + BoxGirl! is HAL Laboratory's puzzle-platform game, released for Nintendo Switch on 26 April 2019. Qbby and Qucy cross small stages by creating chains of boxes from their bodies. Those simple shapes can bridge a gap, hold down a switch or protect a character from a hazard. The fourth game in the series adds a dedicated two-player campaign, giving the same minimal set of objects another purpose when two people must coordinate their positions and the structures they build.

cards.heading: Build only what the obstacle needs
cards.text: Each stage limits how many boxes can be produced in one chain. The challenge is to find a shape and position that solve the obstacle within that allowance. A chain can be carried, extended or set down, so the solution often depends on understanding how its placement changes what the character can reach next. Collectible crowns and rewards for economical solutions encourage another attempt after reaching the exit, turning a route that merely works into one built with fewer unnecessary pieces.

cards.heading: Two characters share the same puzzle
cards.text: A Tale for Two gives both players their own boxes and asks them to cooperate across its obstacles. It can also be played alone by switching between the characters. A third campaign introduces the taller Qudy, whose rectangular form changes the shapes available and the spaces they can occupy. Across 270 stages, the game varies the relationship between body, box and empty space. Its clear drawings leave the movement of those few elements to explain both the problem and the eventual solution.

main.title: Days Gone
main.subtitle: A motorcycle through a damaged Oregon
main.summary: Days Gone is Bend Studio's open-world action-adventure, released for PlayStation 4 on 26 April 2019. Deacon St. John survives in Oregon after a pandemic has transformed much of the population into hostile creatures known as Freakers. Working between camps, he begins to suspect that his wife Sarah may still be alive. His motorcycle connects the places and people left in this landscape. Travel requires fuel and maintenance, making the vehicle a continuing concern rather than an endlessly available means of crossing the map.

cards.heading: A motorcycle through a damaged Oregon
cards.text: Days Gone is Bend Studio's open-world action-adventure, released for PlayStation 4 on 26 April 2019. Deacon St. John survives in Oregon after a pandemic has transformed much of the population into hostile creatures known as Freakers. Working between camps, he begins to suspect that his wife Sarah may still be alive. His motorcycle connects the places and people left in this landscape. Travel requires fuel and maintenance, making the vehicle a continuing concern rather than an endlessly available means of crossing the map.

cards.heading: Prepare before the horde starts moving
cards.text: Freakers can gather into large hordes whose numbers change the meaning of an ordinary fight. The player can use explosives, traps, the surrounding terrain and planned escape routes to reduce their advantage. Starting an encounter without supplies or a working route back to the motorcycle can quickly become a mistake. Smaller threats and human opponents give other uses to stealth, firearms and improvised weapons. The open world therefore asks for preparation on two scales: the immediate approach to a target and the resources needed to leave once the situation changes.

cards.heading: A long road for the studio
cards.text: Camps provide jobs, trading and relationships that draw Deacon across the map between the main story's events. Weather and varied terrain give the same journey different conditions, supporting the central Oregon setting. The project marked Bend Studio's return to an original property after years of work on handheld games, with John Garvin writing and Nathan Whitehead composing. Its launch received mixed reviews, including criticism of technical problems and mission design. A Windows version followed in 2021, and the PlayStation 5 remaster arrived in 2025 with additional modes.

main.title: Blood & Truth
main.subtitle: An action film within arm’s reach
main.summary: Blood & Truth is London Studio's cinematic virtual-reality shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 28 May 2019.

cards.heading: An action film within arm’s reach
cards.text: Blood & Truth is London Studio's cinematic virtual-reality shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 28 May 2019. Former soldier Ryan Marks returns to London and becomes caught in a violent struggle involving his family and a crime boss. The story unfolds through dramatic scenes and playable confrontations, placing the player inside the role of an action-film protagonist. Guns, nearby objects and cover become things to handle from that viewpoint, connecting the spectacle of the sequence to actions performed within the player's immediate space.

cards.heading: Move between cover and handle the weapons
cards.text: Moving through a firefight uses designated positions: the player looks towards a location and selects it, and Ryan travels there. That structure gives the encounter a directed flow while leaving attention available for aiming, interacting and reacting to opponents. Cover separates one position from another, and different guns change how the next group can be approached. Small object interactions extend the physical relationship beyond firing a weapon, allowing quieter moments in the surroundings to support the feeling of inhabiting Ryan's part in the story.

cards.heading: London Studio expands its VR language
cards.text: An interrogation frames the narrative, with Ryan's recollections carrying the player through the events leading to it. London Studio developed the production from its experience creating virtual-reality action, and Jim Fowler and Joe Thwaites composed the score. The result combines performed storytelling with short, legible physical tasks. Its movement system supports carefully arranged action scenes while the headset makes their scale and proximity tangible. Blood & Truth develops the idea of a playable action film around the player's hands, gaze and position inside each encounter.

main.title: Outer Wilds
main.summary: Outer Wilds is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by Mobius Digital and published by Annapurna Interactive.

cards.heading: Exploring a system caught in a time loop
cards.text: Outer Wilds is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by Mobius Digital and published by Annapurna Interactive. The game follows the player character as they explore a planetary system stuck in a 22-minute time loop that resets after the sun goes supernova and destroys the system. Through repeated attempts, they investigate the alien ruins of the Nomai to discover their history and the cause of the time loop.

cards.heading: From a student project to Mobius Digital
cards.text: The game began development in 2012 as director Alex Beachum's master's thesis. He was inspired to create a game focused on exploration in which the player character was not the center of the game world. Beachum led a small team in building the game, first as an independent project, then as a commercial game at Mobius after the project won the Excellence in Design and Seumas McNally Grand Prize awards at the 2015 Independent Games Festival. Annapurna joined the project as the publisher in 2016 and funded its expansion beyond a student project.

cards.heading: Reception and Echoes of the Eye
cards.text: Outer Wilds first reached PC and consoles in 2019 and later came to newer systems and Switch. Its mysteries and structure drew strong praise, alongside criticism of some uneven difficulty. The 2021 expansion Echoes of the Eye added a new location within the planetary system and placed more emphasis on horror, changing the mood of exploration. Both releases appeared in year-end recommendations, and the original won Best Game at the BAFTA Games Awards. Its reputation grew around the way discoveries alter a player's understanding of places already visited, rather than providing a simple sequence of stronger equipment.

cards.heading: Knowledge opens new routes
cards.text: Discoveries let the player approach familiar locations in new ways. Understanding an event or a place can reveal a route that was available all along. Knowledge survives the time loop, letting later attempts begin with a clearer plan.

cards.heading: Following leads in the ship?s log
cards.text: The ship?s log connects discoveries and marks unresolved leads. It helps players choose where to investigate next while leaving them to interpret how the clues fit together.

main.title: Cadence of Hyrule
main.subtitle: Hyrule moves to another beat
main.summary: Cadence of Hyrule is Brace Yourself Games' rhythmic adventure, released for Switch on 13 June 2019.

cards.heading: Hyrule moves to another beat
cards.text: Cadence of Hyrule is Brace Yourself Games' rhythmic adventure, released for Switch on 13 June 2019. It combines Crypt of the NecroDancer's movement and combat with The Legend of Zelda's characters, places and music. Link, Zelda and Cadence explore a changing arrangement of Hyrule while acting to the beat. The familiar task of approaching an enemy gains a musical clock: the next direction must make sense both as a position on the map and as an action within the rhythm.

cards.heading: Read the enemy and follow the music
cards.text: When enemies are present, movement and attacks follow the music. Maintaining that beat brings rewards, while learning an opponent's pattern helps determine which step will be safe next. Weapons, digging tools and recognizable Zelda items extend the possibilities. The overworld's regions are rearranged for each save, while some dungeons are generated again on a return visit. Exploration therefore combines landmarks with uncertainty, asking the player to read a new local arrangement even when the larger purpose of reaching the next temple is clear.

cards.heading: A crossover carried by familiar melodies
cards.text: Danny Baranowsky's arrangements connect the rhythmic system to Zelda's musical identity. Diamonds persist after defeat and help support another attempt, while temporary items and rupees can be lost. Sheikah Stones provide return points and fast travel. A fixed-beat option removes the requirement to follow the soundtrack, and a second player can join cooperatively. The crossover gives the music an unusually direct job: recognizable themes establish the place while their pulse also determines the immediate timing of moving through it.
